definitions.meaning: a jobbing journalist who churns out copy to order
a rough chop or gash made with a blade

explanation.surface: An author is given a share of the takings.
explanation.definitionFit: A hack is a workaday journalist, and to hack is to chop roughly, so the noun also names a gash.

definitions.meaning: a glamorous, wealthy way of living
people living at the top of a tall building have life up in the air

explanation.surface: The rich in rooftop flats live in style.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a fashionable, wealthy lifestyle, and literally life lived at great elevation.

clue.text: Retain alcoholic drink as a memento

parts.note: to keep is to retain
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a bottle of drink as a souvenir.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake is a small item kept in remembrance of someone.

clue.text: Girl takes half-day to jump over the waterfall

parts.note: Sal is a short form of the name Sally

indicators.note: only half of the weekday's name is kept, its first three letters

parts.note: Monday is a day of the week
to leap is to jump

explanation.surface: A girl spends half her day jumping over a waterfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-day' gives MON, the first half of MONDAY. A salmon leap is a weir or fall that salmon jump up on their way upstream.
explanation.definitionFit: A salmon leap is a fall or cascade in a river that migrating fish jump to get upstream.

clue.text: A motorist carries this, but it's not healthy

definitions.meaning: an extra wheel kept in the car boot
a roll of fat around the waist

explanation.surface: Drivers carry something that is not good for them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a reserve wheel, and humorously a band of flab around the midriff.

parts.note: reads like a cricketer scoring a hundred runs but means reaching that age

explanation.surface: A batsman scores a hundred runs.
explanation.walkthrough: To knock up a century in cricket is to score 100 runs; here it means surviving a hundred years.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching the age of one hundred is achieving a century of years.

clue.text: Saw that the cake wasn't decorated

parts.note: wasn't gives the negative not
a cake that is iced has been decorated with icing

explanation.surface: Someone observed that the cake had no icing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cake' only sets the scene, telling you what kind of decorating is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Noticed and saw both mean observed or spotted.

indicators.note: the letters are turning into something new

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Citing a man called Len makes one sound well-spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloquent describes fluent, expressive speech, as articulate does.

definitions.meaning: a fielding position in cricket, square of the batsman on the off side

explanation.surface: A captain signals where a fielder should stand.
explanation.definitionFit: To point is to indicate, and point is a cricket fielding position close to the batsman.

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Lessons in which pupils are told things before the bell rings.
explanation.definitionFit: Genera are biological groupings ranking above species, so they are classes of living things.

indicators.note: remarkable read as re-markable, fit to be marked out again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to come and see an outstanding band.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtuosi are performers of exceptional technical skill, usually players or singers.

clue.text: Scottish girl gives untruth about the dolt

indicators.note: the fib goes around the fool, wrapping it

parts.note: a lie is an untruth
an ass is a dolt or fool

explanation.surface: A girl tells a fib about some idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassie is the Scots word for a young woman.

clue.text: Do not believe there is something off

definitions.meaning: to disregard a claim as untrue

explanation.surface: A sceptic dismisses claims of a cut price.
explanation.definitionFit: To discount a story is to reject it, and a discount is a price reduction.

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in a different way from how they are printed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Dawn arrived in an unusual way, an observer records.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on notes: a piano or organ keyboard is the thing that carries musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano keyboard is laid out in musical notes, so it is a thing furnished with them.

clue.text: Can be revived using this sort of energy?

definitions.meaning: able to be restored or extended again
power from sources such as wind or sun that do not run out

explanation.surface: Something revived by a kind of green power.
explanation.definitionFit: Renewable means capable of being restored, and also names sustainable energy like wind or solar.

indicators.note: a disturbed arrangement of the letters left over
the word sleep loses its ending, its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's slumber was interrupted, and more besides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unending' trims sleep to SLEE, which 'was disturbed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Else and besides both mean in addition or otherwise.

clue.text: One who carves out a career

definitions.text: One who carves out a career

parts.words: One who carves out a career
parts.note: the idiom suggests ambition, but the person's career is literally carving

explanation.surface: An ambitious person who builds a successful career.
explanation.definitionFit: This artist makes a living cutting stone or wood into figures.

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good man
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A saintly figure keeps time to a gramophone disc.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a single pace in walking.

indicators.note: the word for saw goes around the numeral

parts.note: sighted means saw
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone spotted around fifty people being snubbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Slighted means treated with disdain or snubbed.

parts.note: Princes Street is Edinburgh's famous main shopping street
the possessive ending supplies its letter S

explanation.surface: A royal woman owns a well-known road.
explanation.walkthrough: Princes Street is the best-known street in Edinburgh, Scotland's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A princess is a female member of a royal family.

clue.text: Frenchman arranging the loan for a volatile liquid

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman

indicators.note: putting the following words into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Frenchman sets up credit to buy some volatile chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Methanol is wood alcohol, a light, flammable spirit that evaporates easily.

clue.text: Thought about one's being treated badly

indicators.note: the thinking word wraps around the following letters

parts.note: mused means thought
one is I, and one's is I'S, giving IS

explanation.surface: Someone thought about his own mistreatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Misused means abused or handled wrongly.

clue.text: Thick twilled cotton cloth covers the mammal

definitions.meaning: a heavy brushed cotton fabric used for trousers
the pelt of a small burrowing animal

explanation.surface: A heavy fabric is used to cover an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The fabric is named for its softness like the fur of the burrowing mole, whose pelt literally covers it.

clue.text: Intended yours truly to take on a worker

parts.note: yours truly is a way of saying me
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: I meant to employ a labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Meant and intended both mean planned or purposed.

clue.text: Was successful putting a horse, say, inside the truck

indicators.note: the article and the horse go inside the word for winning

parts.note: won means was successful
gee-gee is a child's word for a horse, written GG

explanation.surface: A winner loads a horse into a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: GG (gee-gee) is nursery talk for a horse, and the 'say' admits the shorthand. WAGGON is the British double-G spelling of wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A waggon is an open goods vehicle, as on a railway, much like a truck.

indicators.note: the letters are set at play, shuffled about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone watches otters playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is fodder rather than part of the indicator: OTTERS AT gives the eight letters, and 'play' alone signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An attestor is one who vouches for something, as a witness signs a document.

clue.text: Nearly drunk from a narrow-necked vessel

indicators.note: the word for drunk falls one letter short of complete

parts.note: bottled is British slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone nearly drinks straight from a flask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' drops the last letter of BOTTLED, British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle is a container with a narrow neck for liquids.

parts.note: jack and tar are both words for a sailor
taken as written
to diddle is to cheat

explanation.surface: A man named Jack, a swindler, talks rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A taradiddle is a petty lie or pretentious claptrap.

indicators.note: the shipboard letters come after the party

parts.note: a do is a party
SS stands for steamship, the craft one is on board

explanation.surface: Someone sleeps aboard ship after a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: To doss is British slang for sleeping rough or in makeshift quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: To doss is to bed down for the night, often roughly.
